Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 39-year-old female with 3-day history of profuse diarrhoea, vomiting, fever, and peri-umbilical pain; likely infectious gastroenteritis.

History:
- Presenting complaint: 3 days of watery then very loose stools (≥4 times today; total “lost count”), associated with crampy peri-umbilical pain that precedes urge to defecate.
- Associated symptoms: Persistent vomiting (last episode 2 hrs ago; unable to keep down fluids/food), subjective fever (“literally boiling”), no blood in stool or urine, no rash.
- Urination: Passing urine; last 1 hr ago, colour not noted.
- Exposure: Brother and classmates with similar illness; no recent travel.
- Past medical history: None reported; occasional dysmenorrhoea.
- Medications: Vitamin D daily (dose/route/frequency not documented); intermittent ibuprofen for cramps (dose/route/frequency not documented); oral rehydration salts (ORS) 3×/day for 2 days.
- Allergies: Not discussed.
- Social: Non-smoker, occasional alcohol; lives with mother and brother; graphic designer working from home.
- Gynaecological: Last period 2 weeks ago; not sexually active; no contraception.
- Preventive care: Not discussed.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not measured (no thermometer).
- Physical findings: None recorded (telephone consult).

Impression:
- Probable infectious gastroenteritis (viral vs. bacterial).

Plan:
- Arrange urgent clinic appointment for:
  • Stool sample for culture to rule out bacterial cause.  
  • In-person hydration assessment.
- Advice:
  • Continue ORS; very small frequent sips.  
  • Simple diet (toast, biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, milk.  
  • Monitor urine output; watch for signs of dehydration.  
  • Seek urgent care/A&E if worsening symptoms or unable to maintain hydration.
- Patient to book appointment via support line; may call back sooner if condition deteriorates.

Quality checks:

● Missing/expected elements:
  – Allergy status not obtained.  
  – Complete medication list and doses not fully reconciled.  
  – No objective vitals or physical examination.

● Internal conflicts: None noted.

● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor inaudible pauses but core clinical data obtainable.
